subject: No-train assurance, prompt/response ownership, and cross-border routing — procurement checklist
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@mediq.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: No-train assurance, ownership, and exportability — procurement checklist

Diego / team,

Thanks for the demo last week. Mediq is preparing a short procurement checklist for the pilot and we need a few concrete items to move forward with legal and security: 

- Contractual no-training commitment: can Redwood put an explicit "no-training" clause in the DPA/DPA Rider (no use of our data for model improvement)? If yes, please share sample language we can use in a redline.
- Prompt/response ownership: we need written confirmation that customer prompts and generated responses are the customer's data and that output IP is assigned to the customer under the DPA.
- Operational proof: examples of the evidence you can provide to demonstrate compliance (audit logs showing deletion/export, proof that training pipeline did not ingest tenant data, subprocessors list and access model).
- Cross-border handling & KMS: does Redwood support onshore-only processing (US-only) and BYOK/Customer KMS so keys never leave our control?
- Subprocessor detail: which subprocessors have access to plaintext request/response data, and what controls prevent access?

Procurement timeline: we need answers and an initial evidence pack by EOW (this Friday) to keep our procurement slot. Attachments: I have included our procurement checklist for your reference.

If it helps, could we do a 30-minute call tomorrow with security/legal (I can bring our counsel) to walk through the operational artifacts?

Thanks,

Samantha Cho
Procurement Manager
MediQ Health
attachments: procurement-checklist.xlsx
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-27T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: No-train assurance, ownership, and exportability — procurement checklist

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a short operational summary and our current subprocessor inventory for your legal/security review.

1) Contractual no-training commitment
- Yes — Redwood offers a contractual no-training commitment as a DPA amendment/rider. We can supply sample DPA language that explicitly prohibits the use of customer prompts/responses for model improvement unless the customer opts in. See attached redwood-no-train-summary.pdf for the standard rider text we propose.

2) Prompt/response ownership
- Confirmed: outputs and customer-provided prompts are treated as tenant data. Our standard language assigns output rights to the customer and disclaims independent derivative claims beyond operational telemetry. We will include the ownership clause in the rider.

3) Operational proof
- We will provide an evidence pack with:
  - ACL-limited subprocessor list (attached: subprocessors_list_2026-08.csv)
  - Audit log samples showing deletion and export events (redacted)
  - High-level diagram of our training pipeline with controls annotated to show separation from production inference (no cross-feed).
We typically deliver the evidence pack as a shared Drive folder plus a one-hour ops walkthrough. I can have security/ops produce an "operation-proof-pack.zip" with the artifacts; we aim to deliver within 48–72 hours.

4) Cross-border handling & KMS
- Options: Hosted (multi-region) or Dedicated/Private. For US-only processing we can configure region-restricted routing and onshore-only infrastructure. We support BYOK/HSM integrations for dedicated/private customers so keys remain under customer control. For hosted customers, we provide an onshore routing policy and bring-your-own-KMS options for enterprise plans.

5) Subprocessor access model
- The attached CSV lists subprocessors and the data access scope. Only a small subset (SRE for platform health, infra providers for persistent storage) has technical ability to access plaintext; access is controlled by role-based permissions, ephemeral credentials, and audited access workflows.

Next steps / MAP (proposed):
- Today/Tomorrow: share the DPA rider sample and evidence Drive link (I attached summary + list).
- Within 48–72 hours: ops deliver the full evidence pack and schedule an ops walkthrough with your security team.
- Legal redline: we ask your counsel to propose edits to the rider; we will review and target a mutually agreed text.
- DocuSign: once redline is settled, we can route the DPA amendment + SOW via DocuSign for signatures.

Would you like Karthik or Kimberly to join the ops call? We can do tomorrow at 10am PT if that works.

Regards,

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Diego — thanks for the quick reply and attachments. A few clarifying asks from our side before we schedule legal: 

- Can you paste the exact contract clause text (not just summary)? Our legal wants a starting redline — we need the precise wording for the DPA rider.
- Evidence granularity: will the audit logs show tenant identifiers and timestamps for deletion/export events (we need correlation to our tenant id)? Can you provide a sample redacted log entry that preserves the fields we would need to verify?
- Isolation requirement: does Redwood require Dedicated/Private deployment for the no-train guarantee or can we keep this on Hosted with controls? Please include any delta in cost and timeline to enable onshore-only + BYOK.
- Subprocessor access: for subprocessors that operate storage, do they have the ability to decrypt data (i.e., have access to KMS keys)? If yes, how is that prevented for BYOK deployments?

Procurement note: we have a hard cutoff for pilot procurement signoff on Friday. If you can provide clause text and the evidence pack by Thursday EOD, we can accelerate the legal review.

Best,

Samantha Cho
Procurement Manager
MediQ Health

Subject: Re: No-train assurance, ownership, and exportability — procurement checklist

Samantha — good questions. Below is the concrete language and an operational plan. I pulled Kimberly (Security) and Karthik (Sales) in to help with timeline and cost.

Proposed DPA rider snippet (sample clause you can drop into your redline):
"\nNo-Training and Model Improvement. Provider shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, instructions, or generated outputs) to train, improve, or modify Provider's models or model weights, nor shall Provider permit any third party to do so, unless Customer provides explicit, documented consent in writing. Provider shall implement operational controls to prevent Customer Data from entering its model training pipelines and shall make available to Customer, upon request, evidence demonstrating compliance with this provision.\n"

Auditability and evidence
- We will provide redacted audit log samples that include tenant_id, event_type (export/delete), timestamp, and operator_id. The logs will be redacted to remove any PII values but will retain the tenant identifier so you can correlate events. See Drive link for a sample redacted log entry.

Hosted vs Dedicated/Private
- No-train clause is contractual and can be applied to Hosted customers. However, for the strongest operational assurances (BYOK which prevents Provider-held keys from decrypting data, physical onshore-only control plane, and limited-subprocessor access), customers typically choose Dedicated or a Private deployment.
- Delta: Dedicated/Private carries a higher monthly committed cost (varies by GPU footprint). We will provide a short cost appendix once you confirm expected concurrency/throughput. Timeline to enable BYOK & onshore routing for Dedicated: ~2–4 weeks after contract and SOW signoff. For Hosted with onshore routing + enterprise BYOK, ~1–2 weeks depending on KMS integration cadence.

Subprocessor & KMS notes
- For BYOK deployments, the customer's keys are not stored by Redwood and are never exported. Subprocessors do not get access to KMS key material; access to plaintext is prevented by encryption-at-rest + key access controls. Where subprocessors need to perform operations, we use ephemeral credentials and strict role-based access; any required access is audited.

Deliverables & timeline (proposed MAP)
- Today (sent): sample rider text, subprocessor list, summary PDF.
- By 2026-09-01 EOD: full evidence pack (operation-proof-pack.zip) with: redacted audit logs, pipeline separation diagram, runbook excerpts for deletion/export procedures, and an access-control matrix. Link will be shared via Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Cno-train-evidence
- Legal redline: once you upload your redline to the Drive folder or return edits via DocuSign, we will respond within 48 business hours. DocuSign link for routing the rider + DPA amendment: https://www.docusign.com/link/MQ-3481-dpa-amendment

Cost/ops contact
- Karthik will follow up with a short cost appendix and options for Dedicated vs Hosted BYOK.
- Kimberly will coordinate the ops walkthrough and deliver the redacted log samples.

If that timeline works, I'll schedule the ops call for Wednesday with Kimberly and our security lead. Please confirm an attendee list and a preferred time.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up so Mediq can move into pilot.

Best,

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
